content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the symptoms are not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to double the dose to make up for the missed one. For proper storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the medication is expired or no longer needed, discard it properly according to local disposal guidelines. This information was last revised in August 2024. Please note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Cefepime is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is administered by injection into a muscle or vein as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the medication. If using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the bag at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow it to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw the solution using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the bag well and check for leaks. Discard the solution if the bag leaks. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and continue the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow the infection to return. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, or pain at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before using cefepime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other antibiotics (such as penicillins or other cephalosporins), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefepime may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication passes into breast milk in small amounts but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefepime may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. If you suspect an overdose and the individual has severe symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669.
